readings.title: A Son is Born
readings.text: [Ruth 4:13] So Boʽaz took Ruth and she became his wife. And he went in to her, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> granted her conception, and she bore a son. [14] And the women said to Naʽomi, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who has not left you this day without a redeemer, and let his name be proclaimed in Yisra’ĕl! [15] “And he shall be to you a restorer of life and a sustainer of your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.” [16] And Naʽomi took the child and laid him on her bosom, and became a nurse to him. [17] And the women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, “There is a son born to Naʽomi.” And they called his name Oḇĕḏ. He was the father of Yishai, the father of Dawiḏ. [18] And these are the generations of Perets: Perets brought forth Ḥetsron, [19] and Ḥetsron brought forth Ram, and Ram brought forth Amminaḏaḇ, [20] and Amminaḏaḇ brought forth Naḥshon, and Naḥshon brought forth Salmah, [21] and Salmon brought forth Boʽaz, and Boʽaz brought forth Oḇĕḏ, [22] and Oḇĕḏ brought forth Yishai, and Yishai brought forth Dawiḏ.

readings.title: The Line of David
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 2:9] And the sons of Hetsron who were born to him: Yeraḥme’ĕl, and Ram, and Keluḇai. [10] And Ram brought forth Amminaḏaḇ, and Amminaḏaḇ brought forth Naḥshon, leader of the children of Yehuḏah. [11] And Naḥshon brought forth Salma, and Salma brought forth Boʽaz, [12] and Boʽaz brought forth Oḇĕḏ, and Oḇĕḏ brought forth Yishai. [13] And Yishai brought forth Eliyaḇ his first-born, and Aḇinaḏaḇ the second, and Shimʽa the third, [14] Nethan’ĕl the fourth, Raddai the fifth, [15] Otsem the sixth, Dawiḏ the seventh. [16] And their sisters were Tseruyah and Aḇigayil. And the sons of Tseruyah were Aḇishai, and Yo’aḇ, and Asah’ĕl, three. [17] And Aḇigayil bore Amasa, and the father of Amasa was Yether the Yishmaʽĕlite.

readings.title: Family of Caleb and Jerahmeel
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 2:18] And Kalĕḇ son of Hetsron brought forth children by Azuḇah his wife, and by Yerioth. And these were her sons: Yĕsher, and Shoḇaḇ, and Ardon. [19] And Azuḇah died, and Kalĕḇ took Ephrath as his wife, and she bore him Ḥur. [20] And Ḥur brought forth Uri, and Uri brought forth Betsal’ĕl. [21] And afterward Hetsron went in to the daughter of Maḵir the father of Gilʽaḏ, and he took her when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Seg̱uḇ. [22] And Seg̱uḇ brought forth Ya’ir, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilʽaḏ. [23] And Geshur and Aram took the towns of Ya’ir from them, with Qenath and its towns, sixty cities. All these were the sons of Maḵir the father of Gilʽaḏ. [24] And after the death of Hetsron in Kalĕḇ Ephrathah, Hetsron’s wife Abiyah bore him Ashḥur the father of Teqoa. [25] And the sons of Yeraḥme’ĕl the first-born of Hetsron were Ram, the first-born, and Bunah, and Oren, and Otsem, and Aḥiyah. [26] And Yeraḥme’ĕl had another wife, whose name was Atarah, she was the mother of Onam. [27] And the sons of Ram the first-born of Yeraḥme’ĕl were Maʽats, and Yamin, and Ěqer. [28] And the sons of Onam were Shammai and Yaḏa. And the sons of Shammai were Naḏaḇ and Aḇishur. [29] And the name of the wife of Aḇishur was Aḇiḥayil, and she bore him Aḥban and Moliḏ. [30] And the sons of Naḏaḇ were Seleḏ and Appayim. And Seleḏ died without children. [31] And the son of Appayim was Yishʽi. And the son of Yishʽi was Shĕshan. And the child of Shĕshan was Aḥlai. [32] And the sons of Yaḏa, the brother of Shammai, were Yether and Yonathan. And Yether died without children. [33] And the sons of Yonathan were Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Yeraḥme’ĕl. [34] And Shĕshan had no sons, only daughters. And Shĕshan had a servant, an Mitsrite, whose name was Yarḥa. [35] And Shĕshan gave his daughter to Yarḥa his servant as wife, and she bore him Attai. [36] And Attai brought forth Nathan, and Nathan brought forth Zaḇaḏ, [37] and Zaḇaḏ brought forth Ephlal, and Ephlal brought forth Oḇĕḏ, [38] and Oḇĕḏ brought forth Yĕhu, and Yĕhu brought forth Azaryah, [39] and Azaryah brought forth Ḥelets, and Ḥelets brought forth Elʽasah, [40] and Elʽasah brought forth Sismai, and Sismai brought forth Shallum, [41] and Shallum brought forth Yeqamyah, and Yeqamyah brought forth Elishama.

readings.title: Descendants of Caleb and Hur
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 2:42] And the descendants of Kalĕḇ the brother of Yeraḥme’ĕl were Mĕsha his first-born, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Marĕshah the father of Ḥeḇron. [43] And the sons of Ḥeḇron: Qoraḥ, and Tappuaḥ, and Reqem, and Shema. [44] And Shema brought forth Raḥam the father of Yorqeʽam, and Reqem brought forth Shammai. [45] And the son of Shammai was Maʽon, and Maʽon was the father of Bĕyth Tsur. [46] And Ěphah, Kalĕḇ’s concubine, bore Ḥaran, and Motsa, and Gazĕz. And Ḥaran brought forth Gazĕz. [47] And the sons of Yahdai: Regem, and Yotham, and Gĕyshan, and Pelet, and Ěphah, and Shaʽaph. [48] Maʽaḵah, Kalĕḇ’s concubine, bore Sheḇer and Tirḥanah. [49] She also bore Shaʽaph the father of Maḏmannah, Shewa the father of Maḵbena and the father of Giḇʽa. And the daughter of Kalĕḇ was Aḵsah. [50] These were the descendants of Kalĕḇ son of Ḥur, the first-born of Ephrathah: Shoḇal the father of Qiryath Yeʽarim, [51] Salma the father of Bĕyth Leḥem, Ḥarĕph the father of Bĕyth Gaḏĕr. [52] And Shoḇal the father of Qiryath Yeʽarim had descendants: Haro’eh, half of the Manaḥathites. [53] And the clans of Qiryath Yeʽarim: the Yithrites, and the Puthites, and the Shumathites, and the Mishra’ites; from these came the Tsorʽathites and the Eshta’olites. [54] The sons of Salma: Bĕyth Leḥem, and the Netophathites, Atroth Bĕyth Yo’aḇ, and half of the Manaḥathites, the Tsorites. [55] And the clans of the scribes who dwelt at Yaʽbĕts: the Tirathites, the Shimʽathites, the Sukathites. These were the Qenites who came from Ḥammath, the father of the house of Rĕḵaḇ.

readings.title: The Clans of Judah
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 4:1] The sons of Yehuḏah: Perets, Ḥetsron, and Karmi, and Ḥur, and Shoḇal. [2] And Re’ayah son of Shoḇal brought forth Yaḥath, and Yaḥath brought forth Aḥumai and Lahaḏ. These were the clans of the Tsorʽathites. [3] And these were the sons of the father of Ěṭam: Yizreʽĕl, and Yishma, and Yiḏbash. And the name of their sister was Hatselelponi, [4] and Penu’ĕl was the father of Geḏor, and Ězer was the father of Ḥushah. These were the sons of Ḥur, the first-born of Ephrathah the father of Bĕyth Leḥem. [5] And Ashḥur the father of Teqoa had two wives, Ḥel’ah and Naʽarah. [6] And Naʽarah bore him Aḥuzzam, and Ḥĕpher, and Tĕmeni, and Aḥashtari. These were the sons of Naʽarah. [7] And the sons of Ḥel’ah: Tsereth, Tsoḥar, and Ethnan. [8] And Qots brought forth Anuḇ, and Tsoḇĕḇah, and the clans of Aḥarḥĕl son of Harum. [9] And Yaḇĕts was more esteemed than his brothers, and his mother called his name Yaḇĕts, saying, “Because I bore him in pain.” [10] And Yaḇĕts called on the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl saying, “Oh that <dn>You</dn> would bless me indeed, and enlarge my border, and that <dn>Your</dn> hand would be with me, and that <dn>You</dn> would keep me from evil, not to grieve me!” And <dn>Elohim</dn> brought about what he requested. [11] And Keluḇ the brother of Shuḥah brought forth Meḥir, who was the father of Eshton. [12] And Eshton brought forth Bĕyth Rapha, and Pasĕaḥ, and Teḥinnah the father of Ir Naḥash. These were the men of Rĕḵah. [13] And the sons of Qenaz: Othni’ĕl and Serayah. And the sons of Othni’ĕl: Ḥathath, [14] and Meʽonothai, who brought forth Ophrah. And Serayah brought forth Yo’aḇ the father of Ge Harashim, for they were craftsmen. [15] And the sons of Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh: Iru, Ělah, and Naʽam. And the son of Ělah: Uqnaz. [16] And the sons of Yehallel’ĕl: Ziph, and Ziphah, Tireya, and Asar’ĕl. [17] And the sons of Ezrah: Yether, and Mereḏ, and Ěpher, and Yalon. And she bore Miryam, and Shammai, and Yishbaḥ the father of Eshtemoa. [18] And his wife Yehuḏiyah bore Yereḏ the father of Geḏor, and Ḥeḇer the father of Soḵo, and Yequthi’ĕl the father of Zanowaḥ. And these were the sons of Bithyah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mereḏ took. [19] And the sons of the wife of Hoḏiyah, the sister of Naḥam, were the fathers of Qeʽilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maʽaḵathite. [20] And the sons of Shimon were Amnon, and Rinnah, Ben-Ḥanan, and Tilon. And the sons of Yishʽi were Zoḥĕth and Ben-Zoḥĕth. [21] The sons of Shĕlah the son of Yehuḏah were Ěr the father of Lĕḵah, and Laʽḏah the father of Marĕshah, and the clans of the house of them that worked fine linen at Bĕyth Ashbĕa, [22] and Yoqim, and the men of Kozĕḇa, and Yo’ash, and Saraph, who ruled in Mo’aḇ, and Yashuḇi-Leḥem. Now the records are ancient. [23] These were the potters and those who dwell at Netaʽim and Geḏĕrah; they dwelt there with the sovereign for his work.

readings.title: Hannah's Distress
readings.text: [1 Samuel 1:1] And there was a certain man of Ramathayim Tsofim, of the hill country of Ephrayim, and his name was Elqanah the son of Yeroḥam, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Tsuph, an Ephrayimite. [2] And he had two wives, the name of one was Ḥannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Ḥannah had no children. [3] And this man went up from his city yearly to worship and to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Ĕli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, were there. [4] And the day came when Elqanah slaughtered, and he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters. [5] But to Ḥannah he gave a double portion, for he loved Ḥannah, although <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had shut up her womb. [6] And her rival also provoked her severely, to make her miserable, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had shut up her womb. [7] And so he did, year by year. Whenever she went up to the house of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, she provoked her. So she wept and did not eat. [8] And Elqanah her husband said to her, “Ḥannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
